summary: The blueprint broadly covers healthy human pancreas cell types, but targeted cleanup is needed for over-emphasized progenitor/rare endocrine programs, a mixed neural module, and a few marker choices.

issues.description: These axes emphasize developmental/progenitor programs in a baseline human pancreas scenario with no developmental note. Age is unspecified, so rare immaturity signals are not impossible, but two full progenitor axes may over-weight populations that are not expected as major components of most healthy human pancreas datasets.
issues.suggested_fix: Either narrow these to rare epithelial/endocrine immaturity states with conservative labels and markers, or reduce to one scoped rare-progenitor/immaturity axis. Avoid making developmental progenitors look like a major branch unless the scenario explicitly calls for developmental ordering.

issues.description: The module mixes peripheral neuronal/axon markers with neuroendocrine or developmental transcription factors. ASCL1 can overlap endocrine progenitor/neuroendocrine programs, while CHAT and TH imply specific autonomic subtypes rather than a general pancreas neural-fiber compartment.
issues.suggested_fix: Refocus this module as a general peripheral neuron/axon signal using pan-neuronal/synaptic markers such as TUBB3, ELAVL3, ELAVL4, SNAP25, SYT1, NEFL, NEFM, RET, and PHOX2B where appropriate. If autonomic subtype resolution is desired, split sympathetic/cholinergic markers into separate gated axes rather than mixing them in the core neural module.

issues.description: Most alpha-cell markers are plausible, but GC is not a canonical alpha-cell marker and may introduce hepatic/plasma-protein-like signal. TTR is reported in alpha cells but is also broadly secretory/context-dependent.
issues.suggested_fix: Replace GC with a more pancreas alpha-cell-specific marker such as LOXL4, TM4SF4, CRYBA2, or TMEM176B. Keep TTR only if the intent is to capture a known alpha-cell expression program rather than a strict subtype marker.

issues.description: Serotonergic/enterochromaffin-like endocrine cells are rare and more context-dependent than alpha, beta, delta, and PP cells. As a full sibling endocrine subtype axis, this may be over-resolved for a general healthy pancreas embedding.
issues.suggested_fix: Re-label and tune it as a rare serotonergic endocrine state, or merge it conceptually with a rare endocrine-state axis. Keep TPH1, DDC, and SLC18A1 if retaining the axis, but do not make it equivalent in expected prevalence to the main islet endocrine subtypes.

issues.description: The stromal compartment captures generic fibroblast matrix genes, pericytes, smooth muscle, and adipocytes, but it does not explicitly resolve resident pancreatic stellate-like fibroblasts, which are a common non-epithelial pancreas population.
issues.suggested_fix: Add or rename a fibroblast/stellate axis with pancreatic stromal markers such as PDGFRA, DCN, LUM, COL1A1, COL1A2, COL3A1, RGS4, MMP2, and CXCL12 as appropriate, while keeping pericyte and smooth muscle separate.

out_of_scope: The number of axes is on the high side but defensible for an all-cell human pancreas embedding because the blueprint resolves endocrine, vascular, immune, stromal, and neural compartments separately.
No structural placeholders or orphan module problems were evident from python3 embedder_blueprint.py --describe.
